faqs.a: The upper age limit for most RAF officer branches is 36, with pilots and weapon systems officers capped at 25, physical education officers at 26, legal officers at 35 and chaplains at 49. Aviator entrants can apply from 15 years and 9 months and must attest before their 48th birthday.
faqs.q: What is the age limit to join the RAF as an officer?

faqs.a: Applicants must be UK citizens, holders of dual UK and other nationality, or Commonwealth citizens since birth with right-to-work status, depending on the role. Candidates should normally have resided in the UK for the five years before applying, though a minimum of three years may be considered, because security vetting is mandatory.
faqs.q: Can non-British citizens join the RAF?

faqs.a: The Pre-Joining Fitness Test is a 2.4km treadmill run at a local gym. For ages 17 to 29, men must finish in 13 minutes 20 seconds and women in 15 minutes 48 seconds, with slower times allowed for older age groups. A second fitness test, the multi-stage fitness or bleep test, takes place at RAF Cranwell during the familiarisation visit.
faqs.q: What are the RAF fitness test standards?

faqs.a: Officer candidates attend the Officers and Aircrew Selection Centre at RAF College Cranwell for up to four days of aptitude tests, fitness tests, interviews and an occupational health assessment. Successful candidates then complete 24 weeks of initial officer training at Cranwell before specialist training in their branch.

headline: RAF Recruitment 2026: Officer Entry, Fitness and Selection Guide
metaDescription: RAF recruitment 2026: officer entry requirements, 24 weeks at Cranwell, OASC selection, PJFT 2.4km run standards, age limits and nationality rules.

sections.content:
RAF officers lead teams across air operations, engineering, logistics, medical and support branches. Every officer completes initial officer training at RAF College Cranwell in Lincolnshire, a 24-week course covering leadership, air power studies, military skills, adventurous training and physical conditioning.

Aviator entrants, the RAF's non-commissioned airmen and airwomen, instead train for 10 weeks at RAF Halton. Officer branches recruit graduates and school leavers alike, though engineer, medical, legal and training officers need relevant degrees or professional qualifications.
sections.title: Officer Roles and Cranwell Training

sections.content:
Applicants must be UK citizens, dual UK and other nationality holders, or Commonwealth citizens since birth with right-to-work status, depending on the branch and security requirements. Some sensitive roles are open only to those who have been UK citizens and residents since birth.

Candidates should normally have resided in the UK for the five years immediately before applying, with a minimum of three years considered case by case. The upper age limit for most officer branches is 36, dropping to 25 for pilots and weapon systems officers. All applicants must pass an RAF swim test.
sections.title: Eligibility: Age, Nationality and Residency

sections.content:
Officer candidates attend the Officers and Aircrew Selection Centre at RAF Cranwell for up to four days. The process combines computer-based aptitude tests, fitness assessments, group exercises, interviews and an occupational health assessment to judge leadership potential and branch suitability.

Selection is competitive and branch-specific: pilot candidates face additional flying aptitude testing, while engineering officers sit technical assessments. From application to starting training, candidates should expect a timeline of several months, with medical and vetting checks running in parallel.
sections.title: OASC Selection Process

sections.content:
The first fitness hurdle is the Pre-Joining Fitness Test: a 2.4km treadmill run at zero incline at a local gym. Men aged 17 to 29 must finish in 13 minutes 20 seconds, women in 15 minutes 48 seconds, with age-adjusted times for older candidates.

A second test takes place at Cranwell during the familiarisation visit, including the multi-stage fitness test, or bleep test, with standards set on the day. Physical fitness is tested again throughout initial training, so arriving above the minimum standard gives candidates a meaningful advantage.
